title: All Six Trig Functions
short: Tangent, cotangent, secant and cosecant from sine and cosine.
trouble: Students pair secant with sine because both start with s.

blocks.html: Sine and cosine are the coordinates of a point on the unit circle. Four more functions are built from them. They are not new information, just useful ratios that show up often enough to deserve names.

$$\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}, \quad \cot\theta = \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}, \quad \sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta}, \quad \csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta}.$$ If $(x, y)$ is any point on the terminal side at distance $r = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$ from the origin: $\sin\theta = \frac{y}{r}$, $\cos\theta = \frac{x}{r}$, $\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x}$, $\csc\theta = \frac{r}{y}$, $\sec\theta = \frac{r}{x}$, $\cot\theta = \frac{x}{y}$.

A point $(x, y)$ at distance $r$ is the unit-circle point scaled up by $r$. Dividing by $r$ brings it back: $\left(\frac{x}{r}, \frac{y}{r}\right) = (\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$. Tangent is the slope of the terminal side, $\frac{y}{x}$, and the "co" and reciprocal functions follow. A function is undefined wherever its denominator is $0$: tangent and secant when $x = 0$, cotangent and cosecant when $y = 0$.

blocks.cap: The purple line is $\tan\theta$: where the terminal side, extended, hits the line $x = 1$. It blows up near $90^\circ$, where $\cos\theta = 0$.

blocks.title: All six from a point
blocks.q: The terminal side of $\theta$ passes through $(-5, 12)$. Find all six trig values.

blocks.html: Pairing secant with sine because both start with "s". Each reciprocal pair has exactly one "co": sine goes with cosecant, cosine with secant, tangent with cotangent. Check at $0$: $\sec 0$ should be $\frac{1}{\cos 0} = 1$; if you had used sine you would be dividing by $0$.
